title: Orthogonal spectral bases for the total-degree valuation
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $n\ge1$, $A=F[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. The formula $|0|_t=0$, $|f/g|_t=\exp(\deg f-\deg g)$ for nonzero $f,g\in A$, with total degree, defines a multiplicative nonarchimedean real absolute value on $Q$. Let $L/Q$ be any finite field extension and let $s=s_{L/Q}$ be the minimal-polynomial spectral norm [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Put $r=[L:Q]$. There exists a $Q$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $L$ such that $$s\left(\sum_{i=1}^r c_i u_i\right)=\max_{1\le i\le r}|c_i|_t s(u_i)\qquad(c_i\in Q).$$ Neither separability of $L/Q$ nor perfection of $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/1, printed p.214 (scan PDF p.220), and its application in the proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.217 (scan PDF p.223): total-degree stability gives an orthogonal basis. Primary scan read 2026-10-25; archival literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $D(f)=\deg f$ for nonzero polynomials. By [lem-sfb-mvpolynomial-total-degree-product], $D(fg)=D(f)+D(g)$. If $f/g=f\prime/g\prime\ne0$, cross multiplication and degree additivity give $D(f)-D(g)=D(f\prime)-D(g\prime)$, so the formula is well-defined and multiplicative. In the monomial description [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], addition introduces no new monomials; thus the degree of a nonzero sum is at most the maximum of the degrees of its summands. Apply this to the numerator $fg\prime+f\prime g$ over the common denominator $gg\prime$ to get the ultrametric inequality, treating a zero numerator separately. Exponentials are positive and the separately defined value at zero is zero. Constants have degree zero; replacing a polynomial by its negative does not change its support. Hence $|1|_t=1$ and $|-q|_t=|q|_t$. Every nonzero value lies in $\exp(\mathbf Z)$, and every $\exp(m)$ occurs, using $X_1^m$ for $m\ge0$ and $1/X_1^{-m}$ for $m<0$. In particular the valuation is nontrivial and discrete, with $\rho=\exp(1)>1$.

source.place: Section 5.3.3, total-degree formula and Proposition 1, printed p.214 (scan PDF p.220); explicit verification of the formula.

proof.text: Fix the given finite extension $L/Q$ and any $Q$-basis $w_1,\ldots,w_r$. Apply [lem-trf-degree-valuation-weak-stability] to obtain real $c,C>0$ and $c\max_i|a_i|_t\le s(\sum_i a_iw_i)\le C\max_i|a_i|_t$ for all coefficients. Step 1 supplies the absolute value required by this lemma. Its statement permits arbitrary $F$ and finite extensions, so the inseparable case is included.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.3/1, proof citing Proposition 3.5.3/3; printed p.214 (scan PDF p.220), and printed p.155 (scan PDF p.163).

proof.text: The norm axioms, definiteness and scalar homogeneity for $s$ follow from [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], without completeness. Apply [lem-trf-discrete-weak-cartesian-basis] to the $Q$-vector space $V=L$, the norm $N=s$, the basis and bounds of step 2, and the value group $\exp(\mathbf Z)$ established in step 1. It gives a basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ with $s(\sum_i c_iu_i)=\max_i|c_i|_t s(u_i)$ for every coefficient family, as required.

BGR is not in literature/ (it is WANTED) and the scan has no text layer, so I checked every step mathematically myself; the cited places are BGR 5.3.3/1, 3.5.3/3, 3.6.2/1 and 2.4.3/11. Step 1 is elementary and correct: degree additivity comes from the Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-mvpolynomial-total-degree-product, deg of a sum is at most the max by the monomial description, this gives the ultrametric inequality over a common denominator, and the value group is exp(Z) via X_1^{±m}, so rho=e. Step 2 cites lem-trf-degree-valuation-weak-stability, which states exactly the bounds used. That node is true: |.|_t=exp(-ord_H) for the hyperplane at infinity in P^n, its DVR is excellent, so L⊗Q^ is a reduced product of fields and the spectral norm is equivalent to the max norm. It covers imperfect F and inseparable L. Step 3 takes the norm axioms from the statement of the leaf lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm and applies lem-trf-discrete-weak-cartesian-basis. That node is true: the completion is spherically complete with the full dimension r because of the lower bound, and approximating an orthogonal basis of the completion keeps it orthogonal. Edge cases V=0 and r=1 hold, and the lower bound is necessary. Neither new node restates the item: one is strictly weaker, the other is general linear algebra. Both are statement only and self-contained, with created.item set to this item, correct blueprint.from/via, and grep, LeanSearch, Loogle and LeanFinder searches with real results.
